overall: Atlanta is starting June 22nd under a completely overcast sky (OVC, 100% cloud cover, ceiling ~900 ft) with a current temp of 75.2°F and a running max of only 77.0°F as of 07:30 ET. Warming is underway (+1.3°F/hr velocity) but decelerating (acceleration -0.90°F/hr²) and the heavy morning cloud deck is suppressing early heating. A high dewpoint of 71.6°F and SW winds of ~9 mph reflect a humid, moisture-laden airmass ahead of afternoon convective activity.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful model spread: HRRR projects 89.2°F (aggressive, consistent with the NWS 'near 89°F' forecast), while NBM comes in at 86.6°F and ECMWF at the conservative end at 85.2°F. The heavy morning overcast — not fully captured in some NWP guidance — and the 40% chance of afternoon thunderstorms after 1 PM introduce downside risk to the HRRR/NWS target, as early storm initiation could cap the afternoon peak before it matures.
max_temp_prediction: The META model's mode centers on 88–89°F (30.7%) with meaningful probability extending into 90–93°F, but the current all-sky overcast and decelerating warming trend argue for a slight downward adjustment from the NWS 89°F headline. If cloud cover breaks as the NWS expects and storms hold off until mid-afternoon, a peak near 87–89°F is most likely; if storms fire earlier or clouds linger, the high could settle closer to 85–87°F. Confidence is moderate-low given the high model spread and active convective environment; best single estimate is approximately 87.5°F.
